units.translation: Truly a prophet, and not the fear of dreams.
And at my heart fear is ready to sing.
May I not be greatly overcome by fear.
Let not fear overcome your mind.
In fear of the hawks of the same wing.
For highest among mortals is fear.
Beware lest boldness give birth to fear.
It is no wonder to be distressed by fear in the mind.
Grant release from fears, grant release.
there is no hope for me to walk in the halls
there is no hope for me that fear will walk in the hall
Fear (son of Ares and Aphrodite in Hesiod, Theogony 940).
For passages in Homer and other authors, see Thesaurus vol. 8 p. 966.
They swore by Ares, Enyo, and blood-loving Phobos.
Phoebe, daughter of Heaven and Earth, about whom see Thesaurus vol. 8 p. 970.
Another Titaness, daughter of Earth, Phoebe, sat there; she gave the birth-gift to Phoebus; and the name of Phoebe is derived from him.
Phoebus, the same god as Apollo, who is called either Apollo or Phoebus or by both names together, Phoebus Apollo.
The whole race of Laius is hated by Phoebus.
She gave the birth-gift to Phoebus.
At the hearth of the god Phoebus.
The divine, unlying mouth of Phoebus.
And roasted by the bright flame of the sun.

The disease (love of Zeus) which wastes me, anointing me with frenzied goads.
